definition: An internal model, learned or engineered, that represents an AI system's understanding of how its environment behaves and changes in response to actions.
details: World models are central to planning-capable AI systems, including certain reinforcement learning agents, since a good internal simulation of environment dynamics allows an agent to evaluate potential actions before actually taking them.

explainer.lead: A world model is an internal model, learned or engineered, of how an AI system's environment behaves and changes in response to actions. It is central to planning-capable systems because simulation lets an agent evaluate actions before taking them.

tiers.eli5: Before you cross a street, you picture in your head how the cars will move; a world model is that kind of mental simulation for an AI.
tiers.practitioner: Certain reinforcement learning agents rely on a good internal simulation of environment dynamics to plan. The pitfall is trusting a model that diverges from reality, which leads to bad decisions made in simulation.
tiers.paperLevel: An internal model, learned or engineered, representing an AI system's understanding of how its environment behaves and changes in response to actions; a good simulation of dynamics allows evaluation of potential actions before they are taken.

explainer.example: A reinforcement learning agent uses its world model to simulate several candidate moves and picks the best one without executing each in the real environment.
